RAM MT/s, CAS latency, and first-word latency.

How transfer rate and timing relate, with a simple latency estimate.

01

MT/s is a transfer rate

DDR memory performs transfers on both clock edges, so the advertised data rate is not the physical clock frequency. Higher MT/s increases peak bandwidth when the platform supports it.

02

CAS is measured in cycles

A rough CAS latency estimate in nanoseconds is 2000 × CL ÷ MT/s. This compares one timing only and does not represent every memory delay or application outcome.

03

Platform settings matter

The CPU memory controller, motherboard, module layout, profile support, voltage, and firmware affect stable operation. Confirm supported configurations before buying a high-speed kit.

Sources and verification

Use the exact product manuals and support lists linked from each catalog record. Industry specifications are maintained by organizations such as PCI-SIG, JEDEC, and NVM Express. Product implementations can be narrower than an industry standard.
